corpus.content: Given a string containing digits from 2-9 inclusive, return all possible letter combinations that the number could represent. Note that 1 does not map to any letters.
For N=10, generating all strings using letters 'A' and 'B' requires 10 nested loops: for i in ['A','B']: for j in ['A','B']: ... This approach is rigid and cannot handle dynamic N.
Backtracking is fundamentally depth-first search (DFS) performed on a state space tree that you construct dynamically as you explore choices.
Diagram shows state search tree: root is Empty string. Branching to 'A' explores path ['A'], followed by second level choices ['A','A'] and ['A','B'], before backtracking to explore 'B'.
The base condition for a complete answer is reached when the accumulated path length equals the target number N (here N=2).
In early discussion, the narrator casually mentions that exploring all binary strings of length N takes O(N^2) time.
To clarify, generating all strings of length N with 2 choices per position requires exploring 2^N leaf states, so the actual time complexity is O(2^N) or O(K^N), not polynomial.
corpus.correction_reason: Verbal correction resolving initial complexity slip

corpus.content: The OSI model consists of 7 layers: 7-Application, 6-Presentation, 5-Session, 4-Transport, 3-Network, 2-Data Link, 1-Physical.
The Session Layer (Layer 5) establishes, manages, and terminates connections between applications, handling authentication and authorization (Who are you? Username/Password).
Transport Layer (Layer 4) handles flow control, error checking, and segmentation using TCP (Transmission Control Protocol, connection-oriented) and UDP (User Datagram Protocol, connectionless).
Network Layer (Layer 3) handles logical addressing and packet routing across networks using IP addresses, moving packets from Router R1 in Network 1 to Router R2 in Network 2.

corpus.concept: Data Link Layer Framing and MAC
corpus.content: Data Link Layer (Layer 2) packages packets into frames, handles physical addressing using MAC addresses, and manages media access control across physical links (e.g. Ethernet, Satellite framing).
A student in the Q&A session asked if HTTP operates at Layer 3; the TA initially responded yes before double checking.
Correction by instructor: HTTP is an Application Layer (Layer 7) protocol; IP is the primary Layer 3 network protocol.
corpus.correction_reason: Verbal correction clarifying HTTP is Layer 7, not Layer 3

corpus.content: The gradient descent parameter update rule is theta = theta - alpha * grad(J(theta)), where alpha is the learning rate and grad(J(theta)) is the cost function gradient.
First Normal Form (1NF) requires atomic values. Second Normal Form (2NF) eliminates partial dependency on composite keys. Third Normal Form (3NF) eliminates transitive functional dependencies.
During the live lecture whiteboard demonstration, the instructor erroneously wrote merge sort time complexity as O(n^2).
Course Errata Page 6: The whiteboard capture showing O(n^2) was an error. The actual correct time complexity of merge sort is O(n log n) in all cases, matching the written text.
corpus.correction_reason: Course errata explicitly superseding live whiteboard slip

conflicts.resolution: Verbal correction at 305s confirms state tree exploration requires O(2^N) time, superseding the casual O(N^2) slip.
Instructor corrected TA: HTTP belongs to Application Layer (Layer 7); Network Layer (Layer 3) is IP.
Course Errata on Page 6 explicitly revokes the O(n^2) whiteboard demonstration in favor of verified O(n log n).

questions.query: According to the backtracking lecture, how does backtracking relate to depth-first search?
questions.expected_answer: Backtracking is depth-first search (DFS) performed on a state tree constructed dynamically as you explore choices.

questions.query: What problem occurs when trying to generate length N binary strings using nested loops?
questions.expected_answer: Nested loops require hardcoding the loop depth (e.g. 10 loops for N=10), which fails to work for dynamic N.

questions.query: What is the base condition for completing an answer in the string generation backtracking tree?
questions.expected_answer: The base condition is reached when the accumulated path length equals the target length N.

questions.query: What is the true time complexity of generating all binary strings of length N in the backtracking lecture?
questions.expected_answer: The time complexity is O(2^N) because 2^N leaves are explored; the earlier O(N^2) mention was a slip corrected by the instructor.

questions.query: Which OSI layer is responsible for user authentication and managing application sessions?
questions.expected_answer: The Session Layer (Layer 5) manages connections and handles user authentication and authorization.

questions.query: What are the two primary transport layer protocols discussed in the OSI networking lecture?
questions.expected_answer: The primary transport layer protocols are TCP (connection-oriented) and UDP (connectionless).

questions.query: How are packets routed between Network 1 and Network 2 according to the network layer diagram?
questions.expected_answer: Packets are forwarded across intermediate networks using logical IP addressing between routers R1 and R2.

questions.query: Which OSI layer does HTTP belong to according to the instructor's correction?
questions.expected_answer: HTTP belongs to the Application Layer (Layer 7); the initial TA mention of Layer 3 was corrected.

questions.query: What is the gradient descent parameter update equation in the machine learning notes?
questions.expected_answer: theta = theta - alpha * grad(J(theta)) where alpha is the learning rate.

questions.query: What is the verified time complexity of merge sort according to the course errata page?
questions.expected_answer: Merge sort runs in O(n log n) time in all cases; the O(n^2) whiteboard illustration was an error retracted on Page 6.

questions.query: What is the requirement for a relational schema to be in Third Normal Form (3NF)?
questions.expected_answer: 3NF requires the schema to be in 2NF and have no transitive functional dependencies on the primary key.

questions.query: What is the visual structure shown in the backtracking lecture to illustrate choices for N=2?
questions.expected_answer: A state space tree starting at Empty branching to A and B, exploring descendants down to path length 2.

questions.query: What role does framing play at the Data Link Layer during packet transmission?
questions.expected_answer: Framing encapsulates packets into frames with physical MAC addresses to manage media access over physical links.
